t.d: Water-based colour woodblock printing, best known for ukiyo-e.
t.tech: Design glued to a block, cut away around the lines, inked with brush and printed with a baren; kentō marks register multiple blocks.
t.mat: Cherry wood blocks, gampi/washi paper, water-based ink, bamboo-sheathed baren
t.auth: Technique alone does not date a print, as workshops such as Adachi reproduce with the same methods; early impressions are the most valued.

t.d: Intaglio method of biting lines into a metal plate with acid, from Dürer and Hopfer to Rembrandt.
t.tech: Waxy ground scratched through with a needle, plate bitten in acid, inked, wiped and printed under pressure on damp paper.
t.mat: Copper, zinc or steel plate, hard or soft ground, ferric chloride or nitric acid
t.auth: Early impressions from a numbered edition are valued higher because plates wear; a plate may exist in several states.

t.r: China, spreading to Japan and Korea
t.d: The brush, ink, paper and inkstone of Chinese calligraphy, each with a famed production place.
t.tech: Ink ground from a soot-and-glue stick on an inkstone and applied with a brush to paper.
t.mat: Animal-hair brush, soot-and-glue inkstick, bark paper, stone inkstone
t.auth: Provenance by production place and, for inkstones, by quarry.

t.d: Handmade Japanese paper of kozo, gampi or mitsumata bark, UNESCO-listed in 2014.
t.tech: Fibres boiled with lye, beaten and formed on a screen with mucilage (nagashi-zuki or tame-zuki).
t.auth: Hand-made washi of the three UNESCO types: Sekishu-banshi, Hon-minoshi, Hosokawa-shi.

t.d: Artistic writing in Japanese, from Chinese models to the wayō style and Zen ink traces.
t.tech: Single-stroke brush writing in kaisho, gyōsho, sōsho and kana.
t.auth: Style and school lineage (wayō or karayō).

t.d: Japanese tie-dye by binding, stitching, folding or clamping cloth before dyeing.
t.tech: Kanoko, miura, kumo, nui, arashi and itajime resists before dyeing.
t.auth: Some historic techniques, like original tsujigahana, cannot be fully recreated as the fabric is no longer made.

t.d: Wax-resist dyeing in which hot wax drawn with a canting or stamped keeps dye from parts of the cloth.
t.tech: Wax is applied, cloth dyed, wax removed by scraping or boiling, and the process repeated for each colour.
t.mat: Cotton or silk; wax (malam); copper canting

t.p: documented to the 1930s and revived from the 1960s
t.d: Yoruba indigo cloth made by women with tied, stitched and paste-resist methods.
t.tech: Oniko (tying), alabere (stitching) and eleko (cassava paste); cloth dyed repeatedly, up to 25 or more times.
t.auth: Deep blue-black from many dips distinguishes quality cloth.

t.d: Indian tie-dye in which tiny points of cloth are tied to leave dotted patterns.
t.tech: Cloth is plucked and tied tightly at points, then dyed in stages.
t.auth: Bhuj is known for red bandhani.

t.d: Sashiko is Japanese running-stitch reinforcement that became decoration; boro is the patched cloth it mended.
t.tech: Repeating or interlocking running stitches in thick cotton thread.
t.mat: White cotton thread on indigo cloth; linen

t.d: Wool embroidery on linen with tree-of-life and fanciful plant and animal motifs, used for hangings and bed curtains.
t.tech: Two-ply wool worked in a variety of stitches on linen or linen-cotton twill.

t.d: Norwegian counted whitework with drawn-thread openings in geometric designs.
t.tech: Counted drawn-thread whitework worked on white linen.

t.d: Running-stitch embroidery in which layers of old cloth are quilted together.
t.tech: Simple running stitches, often covering the whole cloth for a wavy texture.
t.mat: Old saris and dhotis; cotton and silk thread

t.d: Aqueous surface design in which colours float on water or size and are lifted onto paper.
t.tech: Colours on water (suminagashi) or on a mucilage size (ebru, Western marbling) are patterned with combs or styluses and printed.
t.mat: Size of carrageenan or gum tragacanth; ox gall; acrylic, gouache or oil colours; washi or alum-treated paper
t.auth: Each print is a unique monotype.

t.d: Japanese mending of broken pottery with urushi lacquer dusted with gold, silver or platinum.
t.tech: urushi lacquer joins and fills, cured in a humid furo, then metal powder is applied
t.mat: urushi, wheat flour, clay, gold, silver or platinum powder
t.auth: lacquer seams cured over days and dusted with metal powder rather than epoxy glue

t.d: Assembly of lamp shades and window sections from glass wrapped in copper foil and soldered.
t.tech: copper foil wrap and solder over numbered templates
t.auth: foil-soldered seams in place of lead came

t.d: Venetian torch-formed glass beads and objects, with fiorato and foil beads as signature forms.
t.tech: lampworking on a mandrel with a torch

t.d: Mosaic from stone and handmade glass tesserae, from Roman opus tessellatum to golden Byzantine church interiors.
t.tech: tesserae set in plaster or mortar; opus vermiculatum for fine detail

t.d: Western floral leather tooling of roses in circular scrolls.
t.tech: swivel knife outlines, then bevelling, pear shading, veining and background stamping on cased leather
t.auth: rose and scroll patterns with shaded detail

t.d: Island baskets woven on a mold with rattan staves, cane weavers and a solid wood base.
t.tech: weaving over a wooden mold
t.auth: rattan staves, cane weavers, solid wood base

t.d: Chair seats woven from coloured tape on Shaker slat-back chairs.
t.tech: woven tape seats
t.auth: tape seat in checkerboard or herringbone weave

t.d: Japanese flower arranging stressing space, line and the relation of stems, often using a kenzan.
t.tech: stems fixed on kenzan pins; heaven, human and earth principles (shin, soe, hikae)
